date_functions.DATEDIFF(SYSDATE, col, 'YY'): _calc_age(col, ref_date)  -- use explicit boolean month/day pattern, NOT tuple comparison

CONNECTED_LOOKUP.description: Port directement connecte au flux principal
CONNECTED_LOOKUP.case_insensitive: If XML attribute 'Case Sensitive' = NO: normalize both sides .str.lower() before merge

UNCONNECTED_LOOKUP.description: Appele comme fonction :LKP.NAME(arg) dans une Expression -- NEVER as apply(lambda)
UNCONNECTED_LOOKUP.implementation: Pre-load ref into dict, use .map() on full column
UNCONNECTED_LOOKUP.multi_output: Build one dict per output column: {key: val1_dict}, {key: val2_dict}
UNCONNECTED_LOOKUP.forbidden: df.apply(lambda x: lookup_func(x))  -- NEVER use apply for unconnected lookup

aggregation_patterns.sorted_input_required: If XML 'Sorted Input' = YES: df.sort_values(group_cols, kind='mergesort') BEFORE groupby(sort=False)

join_patterns.sorted_input_required: If XML 'Sorted Input' = YES: both DataFrames must be sort_values(join_key) before merge

NORMALIZER_unpivot.description: OCCURS=N avec GCID → pd.melt() ou concat de N frames
NORMALIZER_unpivot.gcid_meaning: GCID = index 1-based de l'occurrence (1..N) → devient colonne numerique apres melt
NORMALIZER_unpivot.pattern: pd.concat([df[id_cols + [f'{prefix}{str(i).zfill(2)}']].assign(GCID=i) for i in range(1, N+1)])

ROUTER.description: Split un DataFrame en N groupes selon des conditions
ROUTER.default_group: Lignes non couvertes par aucun groupe explicite (equivalent GRP_DEFAULT)

SEQUENCE_GENERATOR.warning: Thread-unsafe — for Spark use monotonically_increasing_id() or UUID

SCD_TYPE_2.description: Historisation : close ancienne version + insert nouvelle
SCD_TYPE_2.outputs: df_insert (nouvelles lignes) + df_close (SKs a mettre a jour EFF_END_DATE)

oracle_specific.CONNECT BY: ESCALATE -- recursive hierarchy requires pandas NetworkX or recursive CTE translation

null_safety_rules.rule_1_join_keys: Always normalize join keys: .str.strip().str.upper().fillna('__NULL__') before merge
null_safety_rules.rule_2_filter: Always .fillna() on filter columns before comparison: df[df['STATUS'].fillna('').ne('I')]
null_safety_rules.rule_3_case_insensitive_lookup: If Informatica lookup is case-insensitive: normalize both sides .str.lower() before merge
null_safety_rules.rule_4_nullable_int: Use pandas Int64 (nullable) for integer columns that may contain NULL
null_safety_rules.rule_5_arithmetic: Use .fillna(0) before arithmetic on potentially null numeric columns

sorted_input_rules.rule: If XML TABLEATTRIBUTE 'Sorted Input' = YES on Aggregator or Joiner: add sort_values() before the operation
sorted_input_rules.joiner: Both input DataFrames must be sorted on join key before merge

notes.no_apply_loops: All transformations MUST use pandas vectorised operations. Never use df.apply() for row-level logic that can be vectorised.
notes.lookup_as_merge: Connected lookups are always df.merge(). Unconnected lookups are .map() on pre-loaded dict — never apply().
notes.idempotence: Load function writes to .tmp then os.replace() for atomic swap.
notes.null_handling: Informatica returns NULL for unmatched lookups and failed comparisons. Always handle nulls explicitly.
notes.case_sensitivity: Informatica lookups can be case-insensitive. Check XML flag and normalize keys if needed.
notes.sorted_input: Sorted Input = YES means data is pre-sorted in Informatica. Python must replicate this sort explicitly.
